anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet (mcu.kicad_sch) the global-label column beside U1 reads CS0 on pin 6 (GPIO3/ADC1_CH3), CS1 on pin 19 (GPIO4), SCK on pin 20 (GPIO5), CS1 again on pin 21 (GPIO6), and CS2 on pin 22 (GPIO7). Thus the CS1 net is driven from two MCU pins (GPIO4 and GPIO6) that are shorted together and also tied to U3's CS, while the CS0 net (U2's CS) is connected to GPIO3, which the firmware never uses as a chip-select. The thermocouple sheet correctly has CS0=U2.6, CS1=U3.6, CS2=U4.6.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the three chip-selects must be one-per-pin on GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 (U1.19=CS0, U1.21=CS1, U1.22=CS2), with SCK on GPIO5 (U1.20) and SO on GPIO10 (U1.16); no CS net should appear on GPIO3 and no CS net should bridge two MCU pins.

evidence.quote: Each chip has its own independent chip-select: ~{CS} (pin 6) on U2/U3/U4 goes to separate nets CS0/CS1/CS2, driven by ESP32 GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 respectively.
mcu.kicad_sch, label column at right of U1: pin 6 = CS0, pin 19 = CS1, pin 20 = SCK, pin 21 = CS1, pin 22 = CS2 (CS1 duplicated; CS0 on GPIO3).

anomalies.impact: Thermocouple zone selection is broken: U2 (CS0) is on an unused GPIO3 and can never be selected, so its zone reads garbage/never-valid; U3's CS (CS1) is driven by GPIO4 and GPIO6 shorted together, so firmware commands for zone 0 and zone 1 both act on U3 and fight each other, and GPIO4/GPIO6 are hard-shortened. SPI reads of the three MAX31855 channels will not match the firmware's GPIO4/6/7 mapping, corrupting temperature sensing and the run-fault logic.

parsed.summary: The power, heater, buck and thermocouple analog sections match the specification, but the MCU sheet's chip-select labels are mis-assigned: CS0 sits on GPIO3 and CS1 is duplicated across GPIO4 and GPIO6, shorting those pins, instead of the spec-mandated CS0/CS1/CS2 on GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7. This is a connectivity anomaly that breaks thermocouple selection.
